questions.q: A ship sets off on a voyage with three engines, labelled A, B, and C, which work independently. The ship can complete the voyage only if at least two of these engines keep working. The probability that engine A breaks down is $1 / 4$, that engine B breaks down is $1 / 4$, and that engine C breaks down is $1 / 2$. What is the probability that the ship can complete the voyage ?

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Suppose there are two boxes $B_1$ and $B_2$, each having 3 red and 4 black balls. One ball is drawn at random from $B_1$. If it is red, 4 red balls are put into $B_2$, otherwise 3 black balls are put into $B_2$. Then one ball is randomly drawn from $B_2$. If this ball is red, what is the conditional probability that the ball drawn from $B_1$ was also red?
questions.solution:
Let $E_1$ be the event that a red ball is drawn from $B_1$.

Let $E_2$ be the event that a black ball is drawn from $B_1$.

Let $A$ be the event that a red ball is drawn from $B_2$.

The initial probabilities are:

$P(E_1) = \dfrac{3}{7}$

$P(E_2) = \dfrac{4}{7}$

If $E_1$ occurs, 4 red balls are added to $B_2$. The number of red balls in $B_2$ becomes $3 + 4 = 7$ and black balls remain 4. Total balls = 11.

$P(A|E_1) = \dfrac{7}{11}$

If $E_2$ occurs, 3 black balls are added to $B_2$. The number of red balls in $B_2$ remains 3 and black balls become $4 + 3 = 7$. Total balls = 10.

$P(A|E_2) = \dfrac{3}{10}$

By Bayes' theorem, the required probability is $P(E_1|A)$:

$P(E_1|A) = \dfrac{P(A|E_1)P(E_1)}{P(A|E_1)P(E_1) + P(A|E_2)P(E_2)}$

Substituting the values:

$P(E_1|A) = \dfrac{\dfrac{7}{11} \times \dfrac{3}{7}}{\dfrac{7}{11} \times \dfrac{3}{7} + \dfrac{3}{10} \times \dfrac{4}{7}}$

$P(E_1|A) = \dfrac{\dfrac{3}{11}}{\dfrac{3}{11} + \dfrac{12}{70}}$

$P(E_1|A) = \dfrac{\dfrac{3}{11}}{\dfrac{3}{11} + \dfrac{6}{35}}$

$P(E_1|A) = \dfrac{\dfrac{105}{385}}{\dfrac{105 + 66}{385}}$

$P(E_1|A) = \dfrac{105}{171} = \dfrac{35}{57}$

Answer : $\dfrac{35}{57}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider three biased coins. Let the probability of getting head be $\frac{1}{3}$ and the probability of getting tail be $\frac{2}{3}$ in each of the coins. Consider the experiment of tossing the three coins one by one, and the following events:
$E: \quad$ "at least two heads show up"
$F: \quad$ "first coin shows tail".
What is the conditional probability of $E$ given that $F$ has already occured?
